entries.subject: Hubble OPAL Uranus Cycle 33 rotation-A global map
entries.finding: The visible-color surface is the October 2025 rotation-A composite of F467M, F547M and F657N from the OPAL Cycle 33 release.

entries.subject: OPAL FQ727N and F845M maps as false-color datasets
entries.finding: The FQ727N and F845M FITS maps supply two separately prepared false-color observation datasets whose palettes and percentile stretches are declared in the observation recipe; no browser filtering is used.

entries.subject: Unobserved southern region of the OPAL map
entries.finding: The OPAL map has observed northern coverage and an unobserved black southern region; preparation ends the usable observation six rows north of the map equator, fills the rest from a uniform chromatic baseline, and invents, reflects or extends no local feature outside the observed coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A global release observes Uranus's southern hemisphere at this geometry.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL Voyager 2 PIA18182 full-disc observation
entries.finding: The checked PIA18182 full disc supplies the central-disc chromatic baseline that OPAL detail is feathered into across twelve prepared rows, and the same exact bytes are the adapter-owned navigation disc.

entries.subject: Webb NIRCam Uranus portrait
entries.finding: The checked Webb portrait is kept as a visual-composition reference only and is not sampled into the runtime surface.
entries.revisitWhen: A Webb global map suitable for registration and resampling is released.

entries.subject: PDS Rings Node Uranus ring table
entries.finding: Ring radii, widths and normal optical depths come from the PDS table; each ring's opacity is 1 - exp(-optical depth) with no gain. Extremely narrow rings receive a recorded minimum-pixel presentation width while their radii and ordering are unchanged.

entries.subject: NASA public Uranus facts ring colors
entries.finding: NASA's facts page describes the inner rings as gray, Nu as reddish and Mu as blue, in words; no ring color is measured as a value, so the hex colors once made from those words were removed and every ring is the neutral gray of a body without a measured color.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured ring color, as a spectrum or band ratios, is published.

entries.subject: NASA GSFC Planetary Spectrum Generator configuration and I/F response
entries.finding: The reflectance and temperature-pressure charts are rendered at preparation from the checked PSG configuration and its raw 253-sample I/F response at model date 2026-08-30 12:00, range 0.35-1.0 micrometres and resolving power 240; acquisition removes only the request timestamp and elapsed-time comments so the scientific rows stay reproducible.

entries.subject: Pinned photometric phase coefficients
entries.finding: A third chart uses the pinned phase coefficients kept in the package's photometry record.

entries.subject: NASA Uranus facts and the JPL physical-parameter page
entries.finding: The equatorial and polar radii, 97.77-degree axial tilt, retrograde rotation, distance, day, year, temperature, winds and ring count are checked against NASA's facts page and the checked JPL physical-parameter page.

entries.subject: JPL 29-satellite catalogue and the PIA01361 Voyager 2 montage
entries.finding: The source records retain the selected JPL satellite values and keep the PIA01361 montage, with its disclosed incomplete Miranda and Ariel coverage, as pinned scientific source material; because the runtime mounts exactly one detailed object scene, the historical moon billboards and orbit-guide derivations are excluded from the consumer-derived asset inventory.
entries.revisitWhen: The shared runtime gains a contract for rendering a moon system inside a planet scene.

entries.subject: Dated test evidence for this package
entries.finding: The evidence section records that no dated test report is cited in the existing source notes.
entries.revisitWhen: A dated preparation or browser run for Uranus is recorded in this package.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hubble OPAL Minnaert coefficients of the color map per channel (F657N 0.57, F547M 0.80, F467M 0.85), the correction OPAL removed before projection, put back relative to the flood-lit disc centre.

entries.subject: Authored limb lighting: a 0.35 flood-light limb floor, an ambient term and a terminator ramp
entries.finding: Replaced by the OPAL Minnaert law of the color map.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Dated Hubble OPAL visible-color sequence (12 rotations)
entries.finding: One publisher RGB composite per included cycle, component FITS coverage, source-backed map frame and observation dates. Gray grid preserves missing coverage. Current scene lighting and rings remain a presentation, not the historical observing geometry. See the Hubble dates section of the README.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 frames as a sharper map
entries.finding: Hubble sees Uranus about 93 pixels wide (0.04 arcsecond pixels, 3.7 arcsecond disc), so the 721-pixel OPAL map is already an enlargement and only Voyager 2’s 1986 frames are sharper. They show the southern hemisphere alone, and Karkoschka (2015) needed 1,600 of them, each smoothed over dozens of pixels and averaged, to find discrete features. A map built from them would add pixels and no visible detail.
